title: WHERE, NULL, ordering, and limits

spans.text: “WHERE, NULL, ordering, and limits” is a tool for solving a concrete programming problem. Identify the input and desired result, then trace what role the construct plays in the example. Study it not only as syntax, but also for its effects on readability, correctness, resource use, and future changes.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.

spans.code:
SELECT name, price_cents
FROM products
WHERE price_cents >= 500 AND discontinued IS NULL
ORDER BY price_cents DESC, name ASC
LIMIT 10;

spans.text: Returns up to ten matching products, with name as a tie-breaker for equal prices.

WHERE filters rows by a condition, ORDER BY sorts ascending (ASC) or descending (DESC), and LIMIT caps the number of returned rows. NULL represents missing or unknown data: do not compare it with =; use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL. Use parentheses to make combined AND/OR logic explicit.

Key line: `SELECT name, price_cents`
What it does: Returns up to ten matching products, with name as a tie-breaker for equal prices.
Why it is used: Test whether the filter selects the intended rows on a small sample, and handle NULL as a separate case.
If omitted or changed: LIMIT without ordering does not define which rows are returned; add a unique ordering key for stable pagination.

spans.title: Common mistake
spans.text: NULL = NULL evaluates to UNKNOWN, not TRUE, so a row may fail a WHERE condition.
